open_points.subject: repository-port ownership
open_points.text: `models` owns “the repository interfaces”, while each repository section says it owns its corresponding “port” (for example, `audit_repository` owns “The `AuditRepository` port”).
open_points.question: Does `models` own and define the repository port interfaces, with repository modules owning only SQLite implementations, or does each repository module own and define its port?
options: Define all repository interfaces in `models`; repository modules own only implementations
Define each port in its repository module; `models` owns only shared record and DTO types
open_points.default_guess: Define the interfaces in `models` because every repository is declared to know `models` and to implement a State 1 port.

open_points.subject: HTTP request-model ownership
open_points.text: `models` owns “the request models”, while `api` owns “request-body models”.
open_points.question: Which module defines and validates HTTP request-body model types, and which merely consumes them?
options: `models` defines the request types and `api` performs transport decoding into them
`api` defines transport request types while `models` contains only transport-independent data
open_points.default_guess: Keep the types in `models` and make `api` only decode and use them.

witness.initial: A staff expense request contains a field with the wrong type.
events: The HTTP framework asks the route layer for its request schema.
The route attempts to project the request into the shared model vocabulary.
outcomes: One implementation validates once with the request type owned by `models`.
Another defines an API-owned request type and a second models-owned type; their validators or accepted shapes can diverge.
witness.observer: The HTTP caller sees different acceptance or error behavior.

open_points.subject: session and credential validity during project authorization
open_points.text: `authorization_guard` owns “session validity” and “binds a session to its identity”, but `staff_identity`, `viewer_access`, and `service_identity` respectively own session resolution or bearer authentication and produce actor-context DTOs described as evidence of completed authentication.
open_points.question: When a project guard receives an actor context, must it re-read and revalidate the underlying session or credential, or may it trust the context produced by the identity module?
options: The identity module authenticates once and the guard trusts the resulting actor context
The guard re-reads the session or credential and principal lifecycle on every project authorization
The identity module supplies a transaction-bound resolver that the guard invokes
open_points.default_guess: Have the guard re-read the persisted session or credential and principal state, because it owns immediate revocation and the ordered A4 check.

witness.initial: A valid staff session has been resolved into a `StaffActorContext`.
events: A request resolves the session through `staff_identity`.
An administrator revokes that session before the project authorization check.
The request calls a project-scoped read with the previously produced context.
outcomes: The guard trusts the context and the read succeeds.
The guard re-reads the session and rejects the read.
witness.observer: The staff caller sees project data or an authentication rejection.

open_points.subject: producer project-scope authorization
open_points.kind: double owner and unclear call direction
open_points.text: `service_identity` owns A12 and exposes `authorize_producer_scope`, while `authorization_guard` owns “producer grant” project scope, exposes `authorize_snapshot_import`, and cannot know `service_identity` because `service_identity` is on a later dependency line.
open_points.question: Which module performs the authoritative `scope_mode` and `ProducerProjectGrant` check for snapshot import, and how is that result conveyed without violating the dependency order?
options: `authorization_guard` performs the producer-scope check directly and `authorize_producer_scope` is removed or limited to another purpose
`service_identity` performs the scope check before `authorization_guard`, which receives trusted scope evidence
The dependency direction is changed so the guard can call the scope owner
open_points.default_guess: Put the import-time scope check in `authorization_guard` and leave `service_identity` responsible only for scope data and grant lifecycle.

witness.initial: A `granted_projects` producer has a valid bearer credential and an active grant for an active project.
events: The API authenticates the producer and performs any `service_identity` scope step.
An administrator revokes the producer grant.
The same request reaches `authorize_snapshot_import` and then `import_snapshot`.
outcomes: The guard owns and repeats the scope check, so the import is rejected as an unknown project.
The guard treats producer scope as already decided by `service_identity`, so the import is accepted after revocation.
witness.observer: The producer sees a rejected import record or an accepted snapshot import.

open_points.subject: document-read authorization
open_points.text: The shared-facts section says `expense_management` “re-check[s] access and visibility”, but its exact `Knows` list omits `authorization_guard`; accepting an existing `AuthorizedProjectContext` would reuse prior evidence rather than re-check access.
open_points.question: How can `expense_management.read_expense_document` perform the required current project-access check without either importing `authorization_guard` or duplicating its policy?
options: Add `authorization_guard` to `expense_management` dependencies
Pass an authorization capability that performs a fresh check
State that the API performs the only access check and narrow “re-check” to document visibility and project matching
open_points.default_guess: Add an authorization-guard dependency and make the document read invoke it before storage access.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid session and a visible expense document in a granted project.
events: The API resolves the viewer and obtains authorization evidence.
An administrator revokes the project grant.
The document-read use case runs before reading storage.
outcomes: The module relies on the earlier context and returns the bytes.
The module performs the promised fresh access check and refuses the read.
witness.observer: The viewer receives either the protected document or a concealed rejection.

open_points.subject: photo-read authorization
open_points.text: The shared-facts section says `photo_management` “re-check[s] access and visibility”, but its exact `Knows` list omits `authorization_guard`; accepting an existing `AuthorizedProjectContext` would reuse prior evidence rather than re-check access.
open_points.question: How can `photo_management.read_progress_photo` perform the required current project-access check without either importing `authorization_guard` or duplicating its policy?
options: Add `authorization_guard` to `photo_management` dependencies
Pass an authorization capability that performs a fresh check
State that the API performs the only access check and narrow “re-check” to photo visibility and project matching
open_points.default_guess: Add an authorization-guard dependency and make the photo read invoke it before storage access.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid session and a visible photo in a granted project.
events: The API obtains authorization evidence for the viewer.
An administrator revokes the project grant.
The photo-read use case runs before reading storage.
outcomes: The module trusts the earlier evidence and returns the image.
The module rechecks current access and refuses the read.
witness.observer: The viewer receives either the protected photo or a concealed rejection.

open_points.subject: single operation timestamp shared with audit
open_points.text: State 1 says `audit_writer` supplies `AuditRecord.occurred_at` and callers cannot put it in `AuditIntent`, while A28 requires each operation to read the clock once and use that one instant for every timestamp it writes; `audit_writer` names no clock or operation-instant input.
open_points.question: How does the use case's single A28 instant reach `audit_writer` so the audit timestamp equals the business-record timestamps without putting it in `AuditIntent`?
options: `append_audit` accepts the operation instant as a separate argument
A caller-owned operation context exposes the one instant to `audit_writer`
`audit_writer` reads the clock and supplies the same instant back for all other records
open_points.default_guess: Pass the already-read operation instant as a separate `append_audit` argument.

witness.initial: An expense correction will write a new `Expense.updated_at` and one `AuditRecord.occurred_at`.
events: The owning use case reads the clock and constructs the changed expense.
It calls `append_audit` with the specified `AuditIntent`, which contains no time.
outcomes: `audit_writer` reads the clock again, producing a later audit timestamp and violating A28.
The caller passes the first instant through an unstated channel, and both timestamps are equal.
witness.observer: A repository reader or audit consumer sees equal or differing timestamps for one operation.

open_points.subject: bootstrap audit construction and validation
open_points.text: `audit_writer` owns AuditRecord construction, catalogue validation and append, but `staff_bootstrap` hides “account and audit construction” and knows neither `audit_writer` nor `audit_repository`; `staff_bootstrap_store` directly inserts the supplied audit row.
open_points.question: Is bootstrap an explicit exception to `audit_writer`'s ownership of audit construction and A13/A23 validation, or must bootstrap use the writer through a port that remains usable inside the exclusive bootstrap transaction?
options: Declare bootstrap as a narrowly specified exception that constructs the validated record itself
Let bootstrap pass an `AuditIntent` and operation instant to the store, which invokes shared audit construction
Give `staff_bootstrap` access to an audit-construction capability that performs no independent transaction
open_points.default_guess: Extract or expose audit-record construction as a transaction-independent capability and use it before the bootstrap store's atomic insert.

open_points.subject: non-environment configuration ownership
open_points.text: The decision table makes `runtime_settings` the primary owner of A30, but its section owns only “A30's environment part”; meanwhile the shared-facts section refers to `config.*` constants such as `config.persistence`, and A30 also carries fixed Registry paths and other non-environment configuration.
open_points.question: Which module owns the fixed, source-controlled parts of `config.*` that are not loaded into `RuntimeSettings` from the environment?
options: `runtime_settings` owns both the environment schema and all fixed configuration constants
Each consuming module owns its fixed constants
A separate configuration module owns fixed configuration while `runtime_settings` owns environment values
open_points.default_guess: Make `runtime_settings` the explicit owner of the complete A30 configuration vocabulary, including fixed constants, while consumers only apply it.

open_points.subject: staff binary-download routes
open_points.text: `api` says it owns the staff, administrator and producer “HTTP JSON routes”, but the product requires authenticated non-JSON binary downloads, A14 lists `api` as a consumer, and only `api_irregular` explicitly owns viewer binary answers.
open_points.question: Does `api` own the staff-side document and photo binary endpoints and their exact-byte HTTP response construction, despite defining its owned routes as JSON-only?
options: `api` owns staff binary endpoints as explicit non-JSON exceptions
`api_irregular` owns all binary endpoints, including staff endpoints
A separate binary transport module owns both staff and viewer binary responses
open_points.default_guess: Treat staff binary endpoints as explicit non-JSON routes owned by `api`, and amend its ownership statement accordingly.

witness.initial: An authenticated staff member is authorized to read an existing expense document.
events: The staff client requests the document by `document_id`.
outcomes: `api` has the unstated binary route and emits exact bytes with A14 headers.
No module owns a staff binary route, so the request is absent or is serialized through the JSON-route machinery.
witness.observer: The staff client receives a binary download or no conforming endpoint.
